metadata.title: Splitting the Claims
metadata.note: Mycroft patent intelligence progress video 2 of 3. Real build session: claim-splitting regex built and tested against a real BigQuery-pulled patent (US-11791319-B2, 20/20 claims correctly classified), then stress-tested against 3 more real patents (44 more claims). A real false-positive was found and traced by hand (Claim 5 of US-11197952-B2 flagged for multi-dependency, actually a single clean reference).

beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Aishwarya from the Mycroft team. This video walks through building the real claim-splitting logic for the patent Claims Agent, and testing it against real BigQuery data.

output: This video walks through building the real claim-splitting logic
for the patent Claims Agent, and testing it against real BigQuery data.

beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — the real stakes stated plainly
beats.narration_text: Twenty claims, one real patent, one regex. The question wasn't whether it would run — it was whether it would get every single one right.

props.command: claude "split raw patent claims text into independent and dependent claims"

beats.role_note: the build — how the split-and-classify logic works
beats.narration_text: Method: real claims text is numbered sequentially, a claim naming the one it depends on directly in its own text. A regex can split on the numbering and check each claim for a claim N reference to classify it as independent or dependent.

beats.role_note: the first real test result — 20/20 correct
beats.narration_text: Running it against US-11791319-B2 — a real semiconductor patent, twenty claims, three independent, seventeen dependent, including chained dependencies three levels deep. Every single one came back correctly classified, verified by hand against the raw text.

One clean result on one patent proves the code runs — it doesn't prove the logic holds. Three more real patents, forty-four more claims. The parser held up: every independent claim identified correctly, every dependency chain traced correctly.

beats.role_note: the honest catch — a false positive, traced by hand
beats.narration_text: The stress test flagged two claims as possible multi-dependencies. Checking the actual raw text by hand: it was a false alarm. The claim said claim 3, plainly — the flag had triggered on an unrelated or later in the same sentence, nothing to do with the dependency. The dependency parsing was right. The false-positive detector was too eager.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — a runnable prompt, read and discussed
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Take any patent's claims text, run it through the same split-and-classify logic, and check the flagged claims by hand before trusting any of it — a parser that runs without crashing is not the same as a parser that's correct.

props.command: claude "split this patent's claims text into independent and dependent claims, and flag any that might have multiple dependencies for manual review: [PASTE CLAIMS TEXT]"
